newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah buries dead, vows attacks on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah buries dead, vows attacks on Israel.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah on Tuesday buried five of its guerrillas killed by Israeli commandos and threatened suicide bombings inside Israel.

"Israel will witness explosions and suicide bombings inside all of its posts inside Palestine and inside occupied land," Hizbollah deputy secretary-general Naee'm Kassem told a crowd of several thousand at a funeral procession of fighters killed by roadside bombs planted by Israeli commandos on Monday.
A fifth Hizbollah fighter killed by the bombs was buried in Beirut.
The Israeli commandos, in helicopters backed by planes, attacked Hizbollah positions early on Monday in Nabatiyeh just north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

Kassem's threat to attack Israel was issued as Middle East leaders searched for a way out of the latest crisis in Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking, sparked by last week's suicide bombings in Jerusalem which killed 13 people and wounded 170.

"We say to Israel, no peace in the region with your presence of occupation," Kassem said in a fiery speech over a loudspeaker as bodyguards with automatic rifles and ear pieces scanned the feverish crowd.
In Beirut, Hizbollah secretary-general Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah, said Israel's killing of guerrillas would only encourage the group to keep fighting the Jewish state.

"We cannot allow our enemy to use this method to take our willpower. They have been trying to take our willpower for 15 years," he told a crowd of about 15,000 in the funeral procession for Mohammad Hazeema, the fifth Hizbollah fighter killed by the roadside bombs.
"We say to the enemy...We say to the entire world that we love to die," he added.

Kassem also lambasted the recent U.S. decision to lift a 10-year-old ban on its citizens visiting Lebanon and said his radical Moslem Shi'ite group would not abide by its conditions linked to terrorism.
"We will stand with our brothers in parliament against the draft terrorism law which the United States claims to be part of the deal for lifting the ban," Kassem said.
Last Wednesday, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright lifted the ban after Lebanon pledged to fight "terrorism" and sign a convention to work with Washington in any hostage-taking cases.
"Death to Israel. Death to America. Victory to Islam," the crowd shouted as Kassem and other Hizbollah leaders led the funeral procession through Nabatiyeh.
The roar of Israeli jets could be heard, reminding residents who lined the streets and stood on balconies that they live on the last active Arab war front with Israel.
Several hundred Hizbollah (Party of God) fighters in green berets and black uniforms stood guard as the coffins were carried shoulder-high.
Elderly women wailed as young boys carried bouquets in memory of Hussein Qassir, Tayseer Badran, Kassen Kaou'n and Jaa'far Daher.
They were Hizbollah's latest "martyrs" in their battle to oust Israeli forces and their local militia allies from the 15-km (nine-mile) deep south Lebanon occupation zone.

The father of one of the dead Hizbollah fighters was led along the street through the procession. A Hizbollah member told the crowd that the man's son and many others had died honourably and were blessed with martyrdom.
"As this statement is being read, Hizbollah units were carrying out attacks on Israeli forces and they scored direct hits," he said.
Not far away on three hilltops, Israeli forces and their local militia allies manned posts overlooking Nabatiyeh. MG
